newsitem.title: UK: Blair and Hague clash over UK minister's shares.
newsitem.headline: Blair and Hague clash over UK minister's shares.

text.p: A simmering political row over shares held by a government minister boiled over on Wednesday when Prime Minister Tony Blair accused his Conservative opponents of spreading "vile and scurrilous" slurs.

Answering questions in parliament for the last time before a three-month break, a visibly angry Blair repeatedly challenged Conservative leader William Hague to produce evidence that the minister had broken rules or to withdraw his allegations.

The Conservatives, still reeling from their heavy defeat at the May 1 election, have been harrying Labour for weeks over the failure of Lord David Simon to sell his shares in oil giant British Petroleum Plc.
Simon was chairman of BP until he joined the government as unpaid Minister for Trade and Competitiveness in Europe.

Hague accused Simon of avoiding tax by holding one million pounds ($1.64 million) worth of shares in an offshore trust in Jersey and said he should have sold them to comply with ministerial rules designed to avoid a conflict of interest.

Jersey is one of the islands in the English Channel which come under the British Crown but enjoy some financial autonomy and are often used as a tax haven. Avoiding tax via such offshore investments is legal but frowned upon in political circles.
The new Conservative leader, who replaced former prime minister John Major last month, said he detected "a strong smell of hypocrisy from the government benches".
Blair said Simon, who had given up a large salary to work for the government, would have broken insider trading laws if he had sold the shares.
"I don't think there has been a more vile and scurrilous campaign than the one mounted against David Simon," he said, adding that Simon had behaved with complete propriety.
"Because under the previous government there were allegations proven of misconduct they want to try to smear the new government, to pretend all politics is the same.
"Well, all politics is not the same and this Labour government is not that Tory government," Blair said.
